transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... mostly I'm just here because I don't sleep right anymore. I lie there a long time before I can drift off... and then I just wake up. Bad dreams, or just hearing little noises. After that, I can't seem to settle back down. So... that's about it.
For how long have you been having trouble sleeping?
Well... I suppose it's been a while now. Maybe about a year and seven months. Ever since I had a... an accident with a ladder. It started around then.
You mentioned bad dreams; are you having nightmares?

I suppose. But... it ain't just when I'm sleeping. Sometimes if I hear metal scraping... or I just see a ladder leaning in somebody's yard... the whole thing just jumps back in my head. Like I'm right back under there again... waiting for help.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain activities or places because they remind you of the accident?

I guess you could say that. I just... well, I keep finding reasons not to go down to the senior center. And I... I don't really go out to the garage much neither. Specially not near the tools... or that spot where I used to keep the ladder. Just... rather stay away from it, I suppose.
Do you often think that the accident was your own fault?
No... not really. It was just... an accident. The thing just gave way under me. I don't... I don't really look at it like it was my doing. It just happened.
Do you feel constantly on edge or easily startled nowadays?

I guess so. If a... well, if a door bangs loud, or somebody comes up behind me... I jump pretty hard. And my chest... it just keeps thumping for a good while. Even after I see it ain't nothing. Just takes a bit to settle down, I reckon.
Do you try to avoid thinking about the accident or push thoughts about it away?
No... I don't reckon I do. I mean, if it crosses my mind, it just crosses my mind. I don't really try to push it out or nothing.
How much of your daily life or activities would you say you're avoiding because of reminders of the accident?

Well... I suppose some. I just... I find reasons not to go out to the garage much these days. Specially near the tools, or... that spot where I used to keep that ladder. Just don't go in there. And I guess I ain't been going down to the senior center neither. Just... stay home mostly.
How upsetting are the memories of the accident when they come back to you?

Well... I don't know if I'd call it upsetting. It just ain't pleasant. Sometimes... if I hear some metal scraping, or maybe I just see a ladder leaning up in somebody's yard... the whole thing just jumps right back in my head. Sort of feels like I'm right back under there again... just waiting for help. But... I don't like to dwell on it much.
Would you say that avoiding these reminders of the accident is interfering with your relationships or daily routines?

Well... I suppose it's changed things some. I still get up, do my basic routines... but like I said, I ain't going to the senior center no more. And... well, I avoid enough things around the house now that my wife's had to take over some chores I used to handle. I don't really see my bridge friends much either. Just... my days have gotten a bit smaller, I reckon.
Would you say that avoiding reminders of the accident is causing significant problems in your daily life?

Well... like I was just saying, I don't know if I'd call it a significant problem. I still manage my basic routines alright. It's just... my wife's had to take over some of the chores I used to do. And I ain't visiting with the bridge fellas or going down to the senior center no more. So... I guess my days have just gotten smaller. But that's about it.
Would you say that avoiding reminders of the accident is causing more problems in your daily life than the memories or thoughts of the accident themselves?
Well... I don't rightly know which is worse. They both just kind of... are what they are. I try not to think on it too much, honestly.
Would you say that avoiding reminders of the accident is causing problems in most areas of your life?

I mean... I feel like I've already answered this, doc. It ain't every area of my life. I still get up and handle my basic routines just fine. It's really just what I said before... my wife having to take on some of my chores, and me not going down to the center or seeing the bridge fellas. That's about it. Things are just... smaller.
Do you try to push away or avoid thoughts about the accident when they come into your mind?

I guess so. Mostly I just... try to stay away from things that bring it all up. Like I keep finding reasons not to go down to the senior center. And... I don't really work around the garage no more. Specially not near the tools... or that spot where I used to keep the ladder. Just... easier to keep clear of it.
Would you say that avoiding reminders of the accident is affecting your relationships with family members?

Well... like I told you a minute ago, doc. It's mostly just my wife. I still manage my basic routines fine, get myself up and all, but... I avoid enough stuff around the house now that she's gotta handle the chores I used to do. And since I ain't going down to the senior center or seeing the bridge fellas no more... I'm just sort of... around. My days have just gotten smaller. I don't rightly know what else to say about it.
Would you say that avoiding reminders of the accident is something you do almost every day?
I don't really keep track of it like that. I just do what I do... day to day.
Would you say that avoiding reminders of the accident is something that you feel you cannot control?
I don't know about control. I just... I just don't want to be around those things. So I'm not. That's all.
How distressing are the memories of the accident when they come back to you?

Well... they ain't pleasant. Sometimes, if I hear metal scraping, or... see a ladder leaned up in someone's yard... it just jumps back in my head. Makes me feel like I'm stuck under there again, just... waiting for somebody to help. It's bad enough.
